public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 978

*Reference:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/978](https://www.erdosproblems.com/978)
 - [Ho67] Hooley, C., On the power free values of polynomials. Mathematika (1967), 21--26.
 - [Br11] Browning, T. D., Power-free values of polynomials. Arch. Math. (Basel) (2011), 139--150.
 - [Er53] Erdős, P., Arithmetical properties of polynomials. J. London Math. Soc. (1953), 416--425.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial Set

namespace Erdos978

/-- Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2` and is not equal to a power of `2`. Then the set of `n` such
that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th power free is infinite, and this is proved in [Er53]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_one {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Let `f ∈ ℤ[X]` be an irreducible polynomial with positive leading coefficient. Suppose that the
degree `k` of `f` is larger than `2`, is not equal to a power of `2`, and `f n` has no fixed
`(k - 1)`-th power divisors other than `1`. Then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 1)`-th
power free has positive density, and this is proved in [Ho67]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.i {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 2 < f.natDegree)
    (hp2 : ∀ (x : ℕ), f.natDegree ≠ 2 ^ x) (hlc : 0 < f.leadingCoeff)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    HasPosDensity {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 1) (f.eval (n : ℤ))} := by
  sorry

/-- If the degree `k` of `f` is larger than or equal to `9`, and `f n` has no fixed `(k - 2)`-th
power divisors other than `1`, then the set of `n` such that `f n` is `(k - 2)`-th power free has
infinitely many elements. This result is proved in [Br11]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.variants.sub_two {f : ℤ[X]} (hi : Irreducible f) (hd : 9 ≤ f.natDegree)
    (hp : ∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) :
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
If $k > 3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is
$(k-2)$-power-free?

This was disproved by the DeepMind prover agent.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/3b5d6ac2555cd63b83d418c29ff040876be9dee0/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/978.lean#L64"]
theorem erdos_978.variants.allow_fixed_divisors : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (¬ ∃ p : ℕ, p.Prime ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 1) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
If $k>3$ (and $k \neq 2^l$), and for all primes $p$ there exists $n$ such that $p^{k-2}\nmid f(n)$,
then are there infinitely many $n$ for which $f(n)$ is $(k-2)$-power-free?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ {f : ℤ[X]}, Irreducible f → f.natDegree > 3 →
    (¬ ∃ l : ℕ, f.natDegree = 2 ^ l) → 0 < f.leadingCoeff →
    (∀ (p : ℕ), p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ^ (f.natDegree - 2) ∣ f.eval (n : ℤ)) →
    {n : ℕ | Powerfree (f.natDegree - 2) (f.eval (n : ℤ))}.Infinite := by
  sorry

/-- Does `n ^ 4 + 2` represent infinitely many squarefree numbers? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_978.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ {n : ℕ | Squarefree (n ^ 4 + 2)}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos978

reformulations.difference: The first question on erdosproblems.com does not explicitly assume the absence of fixed (k−1)-st-power divisors, whereas Lean adds the hypothesis hp. This hypothesis is redundant, rather than an unintended weakening.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A nonconstant irreducible polynomial in ℤ[X] is primitive. As Erdős explains in [Er53], every fixed divisor of a primitive degree-k polynomial divides k!. For an odd prime p, v_p(k!) ≤ (k−1)/(p−1) < k−1. For p=2, v₂(k!) = k−s₂(k) ≤ k−2 because k is not a power of two. Thus no p^(k−1) can divide every evaluation, and hp follows from the other hypotheses. Adding or removing it leaves the question unchanged.

reformulations.difference: The variant retains a no-fixed-(k−1)-st-power hypothesis even though it represents the uncorrected question allowing fixed divisors. This does not remove any polynomial satisfying its other hypotheses, and it still allows the obstructing fixed (k−2)-nd powers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Irreducibility and positive degree imply primitivity. The fixed-divisor bound d | k!, together with k not being a power of two, rules out every fixed prime (k−1)-st power, by the same valuation argument as for part (i). Consequently the extra hypothesis is automatic. It must not be confused with part (ii)'s genuinely stronger exclusion of fixed (k−2)-nd powers. The fixed answer False is correct; an independent Lean counterexample was verified.

review.notes: Checked all six declarations and found no mathematical defects or stale statuses. The source records parts (ii) and (iii) as open and the cited earlier results as solved. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean verified the integer prime-power meaning of Powerfree, boundary conventions, natural-versus-positive indexing for infinitude and local witnesses, and satisfiable hypotheses using X^d+2. Sign invariance justifies allowing negative leading coefficients in sub_two. Independently proved the negation underlying allow_fixed_divisors in /workspace/review/counterexample.lean using f=X^5+15X^3+24: Eisenstein at 3 gives irreducibility, every evaluation is divisible by 8, and f(0)=24 excludes every fixed prime fourth power. Its proof dependencies contain no sorryAx. Full publisher texts for Hooley and Browning were access-restricted; the relevant results were cross-checked against the problem page, Hooley's published extract, and Heath-Brown's introductory account. The target file was not modified.
